newsitem.title: GERMANY: Camdessus says stability outweighs EMU schedule.
newsitem.headline: Camdessus says stability outweighs EMU schedule.

text.p: International Monetary Fund (IMF) president Michael Camdessus said on Friday that the stability of the euro currency is more important than the starting date of the planned European currency union.
"We must not be obsessed by a given starting date," he said at a meeting of the Christian Social Union (CSU) political party. "The euro should start on an unchallenged basis."
Camdessus said that he was optimistic Germany's "social market" economy could meet the challenges of tougher international competition and that Germans should not be so pessimistic.
"I see reasons to be optimistic. What is needed is decided efforts for structural reform, especially in the labour markets," Candessus said.
Earlier in the day, Camdessus said additional instruments should be added to the EMU stability pact to ensure fiscal responsibility in the currency union.
